core.title: Keep fixed and minimum widths within the smallest viewport
core.given: A styling declaration context named by the profile (such as a standalone stylesheet, a style block, an inline style attribute, or a style object in code), in any file that contains one, outside vendored and generated trees
core.when: it contains a width or minimum-width declaration (spelled per the profile's width-declaration idioms)
core.then: The value, with relative units converted per the profile's unit base, MUST NOT exceed the smallest width among the profile's configured viewports (its default when unset).
prefer: Make content fluid at small viewports, usually a fluid full width plus an appropriate maximum width, not an oversized fixed width or minimum width.
Express wide layouts with maximum widths, percentages, or wrapping layouts.
During GREEN: fix only the element responsible for the current overflow; reuse existing layout containers and responsive primitives.
During GREEN: keep the intended large-screen cap while letting the element shrink.

Configuration (the profile's frontend settings): the viewports entry lists the widths responsive specs render at (its smallest bounds fixed widths); the breakpoints entry lists the widths media queries may use.
avoid: Hiding overflow to mask an oversized element.
Removing useful maximum-width constraints merely to pass the check.
unless: A maximum-width declaration is not judged; it is how wide layouts are bounded.
Custom property (style token) definitions are not judged; they define tokens, not element sizes.
Vendored and generated trees are never scanned (the profile's single exclusion list).
core.why: An element wider than the screen forces horizontal scrolling on every phone.
evidence: The current responsive acceptance passes at the smallest governed viewport.
The affected declaration no longer forces horizontal overflow (established on its own, not inferred from the checker's silence).
The stack's responsive-width check reports no finding for the declaration.
verification: Repository-wide check of every width or minimum-width styling declaration (spellings per the profile) in every styling context the profile names, in any file containing such a context; candidacy is governed by declaration context, not a closed extension list, and extensions only narrow candidates. Applies to all present declarations, existing or new, not only changed ones.

Relative units are converted to absolute units per the profile's unit base before comparison; a finding is raised when the value exceeds the smallest configured viewport width (the profile's default when unset).

The check does not judge maximum-width declarations or custom property (token) definitions, and never scans vendored or generated trees; the exact exclusion classification is owned by the stack's checker, per the profile's single exclusion list.

Enforced with strict disposition (source severity 3); per-rule severity and disposition belong to the rule, not the profile. Detector and validator ids of this rule are realization details; the core names the check generically.

values: any file that can contain a governed styling context (per the profile's styling contexts); candidacy is governed by declaration context, not a closed extension list - extensions only narrow candidates, any file containing a governed context is in scope, and candidacy alone does not show a width declaration exists
files under scanned trees only; vendored and generated trees (the profile's exclusion list) are never scanned

a width or minimum-width declaration (spellings per the profile), existing or new, in any governed styling context, whose value with relative units converted per the profile exceeds the smallest configured viewport width

fires: A styling declaration sets a fixed width on a page container that exceeds the smallest configured viewport width.
A style object in code sets a minimum width whose converted value exceeds the smallest configured viewport.
A pre-existing inline style or style block sets a minimum width wider than the smallest configured viewport.
doesNotFire: A maximum-width declaration caps a wide layout.
A custom property (style token) definition carries a large value.
An oversized width appears only in vendored or generated trees.
A width at or below the smallest configured viewport.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack-wide list of vendored and generated trees that are never scanned.

proposedKeys.meaning: The styling declaration contexts the stack offers (standalone stylesheets, style blocks in markup, inline style attributes, style objects in code) and which file kinds can contain them; candidacy is semantic, not a closed extension list.
proposedKeys.bunValue: stylesheets, `<style>` blocks, `style` attributes and JSX `style` objects, in any file that contains them (e.g. .css, .html, .jsx, .tsx, JSX-bearing .js/.ts, and any other such file)
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No vocabulary key describes where style declarations live; suffix.* is a closed extension list (the rule explicitly rejects that) and idiom.markup_kinds covers markup artifact kinds, not styling contexts.

proposedKeys.meaning: How fixed width and minimum width are spelled in each styling context of the stack.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No idiom key covers styling property spellings; the closest (idiom.markup_kinds) is about markup artifacts, not declarations.

proposedKeys.meaning: How relative length units in styling declarations are converted to absolute units for comparison.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No vocabulary key carries styling unit semantics.

proposedKeys.meaning: Where the stack configures the rendering viewport widths (the widths responsive specs render at; the smallest of them bounds fixed widths) and the default when unset.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: roots.config only names the file that declares roots and profile choices; no key carries a responsive viewport setting or its default.

proposedKeys.meaning: Where the stack configures the widths at which responsive conditions (media queries) may switch.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No vocabulary key carries responsive breakpoint configuration.

neutralityNotes: The convention is inherently web styling: viewport, media query, custom property and relative length units are treated as platform domain language rather than stack specifics, and the core generalizes the concrete spellings (fixed width / minimum width / maximum width), which instantiate to the CSS and JSX forms via idiom.width_declarations. Everything stack-specific is carried elsewhere: the JSX style-object context and camelCase spelling, the candidate extension examples, rem/em at 16px, the atdd-bun.yaml frontend.viewports entry with its 375px default, frontend.breakpoints, and the excluded-tree globs are profile values (five proposed idiom keys plus roots.excluded); the bun_responsive_detector validator id is bunOnly. Bun's path_glob activation fact has no counterpart in the closed fact-kind enum, so it is represented as a file_kind scope fact and as the verification exclusion. Strict disposition and severity 3 stay in core:verification, not in the profile.
